summary.short: IRS final regulations implementing 25% advanced manufacturing investment tax credit (section 48D) for U.S. semiconductor facilities, setting eligibility, qualified property and construction-start rules, and a 10-year recapture rule for material expansion of semiconductor capacity in foreign countries of concern. Applies to property placed in service after December 31, 2022.
summary.long: Final Treasury/IRS regulations (TD 10009, published 23 October 2024) under sections 48D and 50 of the Internal Revenue Code, implementing the advanced manufacturing investment credit added by section 107 of the CHIPS Act of 2022. The credit equals 25 percent of the qualified investment in an advanced manufacturing facility of an eligible taxpayer, for qualified property placed in service after 31 December 2022. No credit is allowed for property whose construction begins after 31 December 2026. Qualified property is tangible depreciable property integral to the operation of the facility, constructed or reconstructed by the taxpayer or acquired with original use commencing with the taxpayer; buildings used for offices and administrative functions are excluded. A facility qualifies if its primary purpose, measured by more than 50 percent of potential output, is manufacturing semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment. An eligible taxpayer is not a foreign entity of concern and has made no applicable transaction in the taxable year. The rules define semiconductor, semiconductor manufacturing and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and set beginning-of-construction tests (physical work test, five percent safe harbor, continuity requirement). Under section 50(a), an applicable transaction, including a significant transaction involving material expansion of semiconductor capacity in a foreign country of concern, made before the end of the 10-year period after placing property in service triggers recapture of the credit; legacy semiconductors are excepted. The regulations cross-reference elective payment rules in section 1.48D-6.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the preamble through § 1.48D–5(a)(3)(ii); § 1.48D–5(a)(3)(iii) onward and the remaining sections are in part 2. Relations and entities are coded only where the text states them. Unregistered targets carry an empty target_instrument_id and are named in target_text. The example companies X Corp, Y Corp and Z Corp are hypothetical and are not coded as entities. Internal inconsistency: the § 1.48D–4(d) applicability date reads 'during a taxable year ending on or October 23, 2024', missing 'after', whereas §§ 1.48D–1(d) and 1.48D–2(q) read 'on or after'. The preamble says § 1.48D–6 is not adopted here, but § 1.48D–1(a) and § 1.48D–2(a) still refer to §§ 1.48D–6. Both relations and entities sections are populated, so their section_status entries are not used. Part 2 of 2: covers the end of the beginning-of-construction rules (para. (a)(3)(v) to (f)), the § 1.50–0 table of contents (which lists §§ 1.50–1 and 1.50–2, of which only § 1.50–2 is in this part), the § 1.50–2 recapture rules and the signature block. Named taxpayers and projects in the examples (X Corp, ABCD partnership, Projects A to D) are hypothetical and are not coded as entities. The Code, the CHIPS Act and the Commerce regulations are cross-referenced but are not in this document. No internal inconsistency was found in this part.

The term eligible taxpayer means any taxpayer that
The term applicable transaction has the meaning provided in section 50(a)(6) and § 1.50–2.
The term foreign entity has the same meaning as provided in 15 CFR 231.103.
The term foreign entity of concern has the same meaning as provided in 15 CFR 231.104.

The term semiconductor means, consistent with 15 CFR 231.115, an integrated electronic device or system most commonly manufactured using materials such as, but not limited to, silicon, silicon carbide, or III–V compounds

The term semiconductor manufacturing and the term manufacturing of semiconductors are synonymous and mean, consistent with 15 CFR 231.116, semiconductor wafer production, semiconductor fabrication, or semiconductor packaging.
Semiconductor wafer production includes the processes of growing single-crystal ingots and boules, wafer slicing, etching and polishing, bonding, cleaning, epitaxial deposition, and metrology.
Semiconductor fabrication includes the process of forming devices such as transistors, poly capacitors, nonmetal resistors, and diodes
Semiconductor packaging means the process of enclosing a semiconductor in a protective container (package) and providing external power and signal connectivity for the assembled integrated circuit

The term semiconductor manufacturing equipment means the highly engineered and specialized equipment used in the manufacturing of semiconductors as defined in paragraph (g) of this section and the subsystems that enable or are incorporated into the manufacturing equipment.
The term manufacturing of semiconductor manufacturing equipment means the physical production (in a manufacturing facility) of semiconductor manufacturing equipment
The term placed in service has the same meaning as provided in § 1.46–3(d).
With respect to any qualified property, the term basis has the same meaning as provided in § 1.46–3(c).

the term qualified investment with respect to an advanced manufacturing facility means, for any taxable year, the basis of any qualified property that is part of an advanced manufacturing facility and placed in service by the taxpayer during the taxable year.
The term beginning of construction has the meaning provided in § 1.48D–5.
The term qualified property means tangible depreciable property that is part of, and integral to, the operation of an advanced manufacturing facility

enforcement.cure_period: 45 days after a determination and notice by the Commissioner, if the applicable transaction is ceased or abandoned (per § 1.50–2(a)(2))

evidence.quote: is increased by 100 percent of the applicable transaction recapture amount

enforcement.triggered_by: Taxpayer engages in an applicable transaction during a taxable year
enforcement.max_penalty_text: ineligible for the section 48D credit for that taxable year
enforcement.cure_period: Exception in § 1.50–2(a)(2) states it does not apply to paragraph (a)(1): 45 days after determination and notice by the Commissioner, if ceased or abandoned

evidence.quote: and is ineligible for the section 48D credit for that taxable year.
